claims.text: Combining noncollinear spin treatments, beyond-DFT corrections, and longitudinal spin fluctuations with spin-polarized DFT will improve predictions of ferromagnetic ground states in transition-metal-based systems.
The target material may be a paramagnetic transition-metal-based high-entropy alloy.
The target compound is near a magnetic phase transition at low temperature.
The proposed method includes noncollinear spin treatments.
The proposed method includes many-body corrections beyond DFT.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations can be incorporated into a first-principles treatment of a transition-metal high-entropy alloy.
At low-temperature ground-state conditions, thermal fluctuations are minimized and intrinsic magnetic ordering can emerge.
Noncollinear spin arrangements and enhanced exchange-correlation treatments capture subtle exchange interactions.
Longitudinal spin-fluctuation treatments represent fluctuations in the magnitude of species-resolved magnetic moments.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations induce sizable moments for Co, Cr, and Ni in paramagnetic CoCrFeMnNi.
The combined treatment captures many-body quantum effects and exchange interactions that stabilize ferromagnetic alignment.
Standard DFT often underestimates the interactions responsible for ferromagnetic alignment.
The refined framework will predict a robust ferromagnetic ground state.
The refined framework will predict emergent magnetic moments that agree more closely with experiment than conventional DFT predictions.
Standard spin-polarized DFT without longitudinal-spin-fluctuation or noncollinear corrections can fail to capture subtle emergent magnetic order.
The method is expected to be most effective for metallic systems with significant exchange interactions.
Quantitative magnetic-moment predictions may depend on the exchange-correlation functional and other treatment details.
